# GEMINI AI INSTRUCTIONS
# Generated by VibeTags | https://github.com/PIsberg/vibetags

## CORE FUNCTIONALITY (EXTREME CAUTION)
The following elements are well-tested core components. Make changes with extreme caution:

- `se.deversity.asynctest.agent.AsyncTestAgent`: Sensitivity: Critical. Note: The INSTALLED gate must stay at-most-once per JVM: every entry point (premain, agentmain, selfAttach) races on the same compareAndSet, and a second transformer would double-weave accesses and double-count every one. premain installs without retransformation because classes are woven as they load; agentmain must keep RETRANSFORMATION + disableClassFormatChanges(), which is only safe while no weaver adds a member, and there are four besides the Advice, which is a method-entry prologue. FieldAccessWeaver inserts a stack-neutral, branch-free call before each field instruction, a load of the monitor plus a call at the entry of a synchronized method and before each of its returns (#822), a DUP of the monitor, an ALOAD of the local the owner was loaded from, an LDC of the field and a call before a MONITORENTER whose monitor the four instructions before it read from an instance field (ALOAD, GETFIELD, DUP, ASTORE, with no label between, #793), a DUP plus call after a VarHandle reference getAndSet it does not substitute (the ownership take, #555), DUP2 and SWAP plus a call before a JCTools offer, and a DUP before plus DUP_X1 and SWAP plus a call after a JCTools poll (#664), a copy of owner and value plus a call before a volatile field store and after a volatile field load, with a DUP of the receiver before an instance load (#742), and replaces an int VarHandle, AtomicIntegerFieldUpdater, AtomicBoolean or AtomicInteger store, swap or value-returning release, or a reference-slot store or getAndSet on an AtomicReference, its updater, its array or an instance-field VarHandle, or an acquiring reference read, an AtomicReference get or getAcquire, an updater get, an AtomicReferenceArray get or getAcquire or a VarHandle getVolatile or getAcquire (the acquire of the store it returned, #741), or an AtomicStampedReference get, getReference, set, compareAndSet, weakCompareAndSet or attemptStamp (#817), with a static hook consuming the same stack and returning the same result, plus one POP where a VarHandle call site declared a void result and one CHECKCAST to the declared type after a VarHandle reference getAndSet or acquiring read (the spinlock, #554, #558, #658, #667; the ownership offer and take, #664). CollectionAccessWeaver replaces each call its tables list with a static hook consuming the same stack, and inserts only the monitor loads and the loop back-edge call its own rules describe. ThreadConstructionWeaver inserts a DUP plus a call after the constructor call of a new Thread(...), and an ALOAD 0 plus a call after a Thread subclass constructor's superclass call (#737). ConstructionWeaver inserts a call that consumes and returns the order argument before a LinkedHashMap(int, float, boolean) constructor call and a DUP or an ALOAD 0 plus a call after it (#807), and an ALOAD 0, an LDC of the class name and a call before each RETURN of a constructor and after a this(...) delegation (#791); it leaves alone a class in a named module that cannot read the library. So frames stay valid and only maxStack grows (COMPUTE_MAXS, never COMPUTE_FRAMES, which would load classes from inside the agent). In every mode, install and the transformer open java.util.concurrent.locks, and with fields=true also java.util.concurrent.atomic, to one module per woven loader and to nothing else: the module of the TelemetryRegistry copy that loader resolves, never the woven loader or its ancestors as such (UpdaterAccess, #659, #668, #855); the locks opening lets the library read a ReentrantLock owner at analysis. In every mode, a woven class in a named module gets a read edge to the library copy its loader resolves (UpdaterAccess.letRead, #862): the JVM's own edge for a transformed class reaches only the agent loader's unnamed module. The library resolves an updater bound before the attach by reading the JDK implementation from that copy (JdkUpdaterShapeCanaryTest pins the shape it reads), and the opening must fail silently like the rest of install. Nothing may throw out of premain — an exception there aborts JVM startup, which is why install() catches Throwable and releases the gate rather than propagating. The Premain-Class / Agent-Class manifest entries live in this module's jar, which is why attaching uses -javaagent:async-test-agent.jar.
